extracted.intended_audience: social work researchers/authors who want to archive or share papers on SocArXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for social work authors on uploading papers to SocArXiv, what types of manuscript versions are acceptable, licensing choices, and the moderation criteria the platform uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to upload a paper
rubrics_metrics.description: You can go straight to SocArXiv.org and click on “Add a Preprint,” and follow the instructions. (If you haven’t yet, you will need to create a free account on the Open Science Framework as part of that process.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'Add a Preprint' flow on SocArXiv/OSF; there is a basic how-to guide and a video tutorial linked from the page. Follow the on-screen instructions in the OSF account to complete submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline tagging—add 'social work'
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sure to add “social work” as a discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filling metadata/tags for your preprint, include 'social work' to ensure correct discovery and categorization on SocArXiv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content — working papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Working papers: Any draft of a paper that is ready to share with interested parties, but has not yet been peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working papers are appropriate for sharing with colleagues, conferences, or journals prior to (or instead of) formal peer review; posting can widen the circle of feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content — preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints: Most people use this term to refer to completed papers that have not yet been peer reviewed (like working papers). However, by some definitions this includes versions of a paper that have been peer reviewed but are not yet published by a journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SocArXiv will host preprints under either interpretation—i.e., manuscripts prior to peer review or peer-reviewed but not yet formally published versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content — post-prints
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-prints: After a paper has been published by a journal, this is a version that you elect to share on our open platform. It may be a version that does not include the journal’s formatting or other changes, or it may be the publisher’s copy (or 'version of record') if you have the right to distribute it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use post-prints to make paywalled publications openly accessible when you have the rights; note differences between author's accepted manuscript and publisher-formatted version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing options
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv offers three options: No license; CC-0 1.0 Universal (public domain waiver); CC-BY Attribution 4.0 International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both CC options allow reuse, adaptation, copying, and distribution, including commercially. CC-0 donates the work to the public domain (no permission required). CC-BY lets the author retain copyright and requires credit and a link to the license. Choose the option that fits your openness and attribution preferences. (Links to more licensing info provided.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation process overview
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers are moderated before they appear on SocArXiv, a process we expect to take less than two days. Our policy involves a five-point checklist...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are reviewed for basic suitability (see five-point checklist). Moderation is not a full copyright check; see detailed moderation policy link for procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation criterion — scholarly
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation checklist item (1): papers are scholarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be scholarly in nature (i.e., research-oriented, evidence-based, or fitting academic conventions). Non-scholarly content may be rejected in moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation criterion — in supported research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation checklist item (2): papers are in research areas that we support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your submission fits within SocArXiv's social-science-focused scope; consult SocOpen.org/SocArXiv subject coverage if unsure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation criterion — plausibly categorized
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation checklist item (3): papers are plausibly categorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate metadata, keywords, and subject classification so moderators and users can find and assess the work's topical fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation criterion — correctly attributed
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation checklist item (4): papers are correctly attributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure authorship metadata is accurate and that contributors are properly credited to avoid moderation problems related to misattribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation criterion — in languages that SocArXiv moderates
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderation checklist item (5): papers are in languages that we moderate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit in a language supported by SocArXiv moderation processes; check the platform for the list of moderated languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right-to-share requirement (copyright note)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition, we seek to accept only papers that authors have the right to share, although we do not check copyrights in the moderation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure they have distribution rights for the version being posted (especially for publisher-formatted versions), because SocArXiv does not perform copyright clearance during moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of using SocArXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits include: Stable, persistent URL to use in your CV/professional portfolio/citations; download statistics; getting your work out faster than traditional publishing; one place to store many outputs and materials for each project; promoting 'social science without walls' by supporting open access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These benefits explain motivations for depositing work (visibility, metrics, speed, archival storage, and support for open infrastructure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal and organizational status of SocArXiv
rubrics_metrics.description: SocArXiv is a partner of the nonprofit Center for Open Science (COS), and SocArXiv as a web platform is hosted on the OSF Framework. As a legal entity, SocArXiv is an administrative unit at University of Maryland, College Park (UMD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMD administers grants/donations and provides fiscal oversight; a Steering Committee and volunteer working groups advise/manage the project. This is relevant to authors assessing platform governance and sustainability.
